newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil stable, demand meagre.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil stable, demand meagre.

text.p: European heating oil and low sulphur diesel were steady on Thursday in thin volume and traders said falling screen values were slowing demand.
Front month July IPE gas oil futures last traded $3 a tonne lower at $164.50. August ended $3.25 lower at $164.50.
A cargo of German-quality 0.2 percent heating changed hands at July IPE +$3.25 cif NWE for delivery by July 10 to 15.
One trader said it appeared the buyer may have needed to cover a very prompt requirement and fair value was at least a dollar closer to the screen.
German quality heating oil for delivery in the second half of July was assessed at around screen flat.
A cargo of low sulphur diesel was firmly offered at August IPE +$5.50 and bid at $4. While the buyer was seen willing to move higher the seller was heard insisting on the opening offer.
The 20,000 tonne cargo with +5 cloud and -2 cold filter pour point is for delivery at Le Havre July 16-25 with options for Hamburg and Bordeaux.
Demand is generally slack following some precautionary buying ahead of the British budget. The only recent European arb play, from the Mediterranean to NWE, is virtually closed.
